name: Pomegranate extract
lead: Pomegranate extract is a concentrate of polyphenols obtained from the fruit, peel or seeds of Punica granatum, a tree native to the region spanning the Caucasus and the Iranian plateau [1]. It is sold as an oral supplement and used in skincare as an antioxidant, with marketing built on its ellagitannin content.

The most abundant phytochemicals in the juice are ellagitannins, also called punicalagins, together with anthocyanins such as delphinidin and cyanidin [1]. After ingestion, gut bacteria convert ellagitannins to urolithins, and people differ in which urolithin "metabotype" they produce [2][3].

Laboratory studies show antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activity [4][5], and a 2024 review of pomegranate extract and inflammaging noted that its studies mainly concern neurodegenerative and skin conditions [13]. A 2026 randomized trial of a standardized extract in 64 women with facial hyperpigmentation reported skin-related outcomes, including hydration and elasticity, described below [12]. Wikipedia notes that research data are limited and that the US FDA and FTC have taken action over unproven health claims made by one major pomegranate juice marketer [1].

paras: Pomegranate was domesticated roughly 5,000 years ago in ancient Iran and has a long place in cuisine and religious symbolism across Persian, Egyptian and Mediterranean cultures [1]. Beyond the juice, the peel is rich in polyphenols, condensed tannins and catechins, which makes it a source for supplement extracts, while the seed oil is high in punicic acid [1].

Pomegranate extract is promoted for antioxidant support, sun-related skin aging and a brighter complexion, both as a pill and in serums and creams. Supplement makers describe the concept as beauty-from-within: ellagitannins and anthocyanins are absorbed or converted by gut bacteria into urolithins, and the resulting metabolites are thought to act on oxidative stress and inflammation that contribute to skin aging [2][3][13]. A representative of the extract's manufacturer said of the 2026 trial that the findings highlight the extract's potential for beauty-from-within applications [12].

A 2022 review of Punica granatum plant extracts catalogues the pharmacological activities and molecular mechanisms reported for them [14]. Beyond skin, pomegranate extract appears in oral-care research, including a randomized trial of a pomegranate extract in a polyphosphate-fluoride mouthwash and enamel demineralization [16], and in studies of fatigue [15].

A pomegranate extract and its metabolite urolithin A reduced inflammation in a rat colitis model [2]. A separate rat study found that an ellagic acid-enriched extract attenuated chronic colonic inflammation [7]. Anthocyanidins from the fruit showed free-radical scavenging in a chemical assay [4]. In healthy volunteers, a standardized extract was studied for absorption, metabolism and antioxidant effects of its polyphenols [5]. Individual variation in gut microbiota metabolism of ellagitannins into urolithin metabotypes has been linked with differences in cardiometabolic biomarker responses [3][8]. Pomegranate ellagitannin-derived metabolites were reported to inhibit prostate cancer cell growth and localize to mouse prostate tissue [9].

In February 2010 the FDA sent a warning letter to POM Wonderful for making unproven claims about disease effects, and in 2016 the Federal Trade Commission ruled that the company could not make certain health claims in advertising; these actions concerned marketing claims, not safety [1].

Human work includes pharmacokinetics, cardiometabolic markers and, more recently, skin outcomes. A randomized clinical trial grouped overweight and obese participants by urolithin metabotype to explain variability in cardiovascular risk biomarker responses to pomegranate [3]. A study in healthy volunteers examined absorption and antioxidant effects of an extract [5]. Registered trials include a phase 1 pharmacokinetic study in 20 healthy subjects [10] and a trial in colorectal cancer patients [11].

A randomized, triple-blind, placebo-controlled trial published in Scientific Reports in 2026 enrolled 64 women aged 30 to 65 with hyperpigmented facial spots. Participants took a standardized pomegranate extract (Pomanox, made by Euromed) at one of two dose levels or placebo for 12 weeks. According to trade coverage, the change in the melanin index of a facial spot, the primary outcome, was not statistically significant for the extract overall; the lower-dose group showed a significant decrease in melanin index change versus placebo at week 12 and significantly higher hydration, both doses increased elasticity, and differences appeared by week 4. Gut microbiota changes were exploratory. The authors called for larger, adequately powered trials, and the extract was supplied by Euromed [12].
A registered trial of 75 participants on pomegranate and skin aging and inflammation, with conditions of skin photoaging and inflammation, was completed; its results have not been published [6].

A randomized, double-blind trial of a supplement combining a chemically characterized pomegranate extract with B and C vitamins was run in people with prolonged fatigue [15]. A randomized trial of a polyphosphate-fluoride mouthwash with pomegranate extract examined enamel demineralization [16].

card.summary: An ellagitannin-rich antioxidant extract with plenty of lab data and no confirmed skin-appearance results.
card.aka: Punica granatum extract, punicalagin, ellagitannin extract
card.note: Regulators have acted against unproven disease claims by a major juice marketer.

quick.overview:
Pomegranate extract concentrates the fruit's polyphenols, mainly ellagitannins, and is sold as a supplement and as an antioxidant ingredient in skincare.
Most research is in cells, rodents and metabolic studies in people. A trial on skin aging is registered, but no skin-appearance result has been published.
quick.mechanism: Ellagitannins are broken down by gut bacteria into urolithins, which are studied for anti-inflammatory activity. Anthocyanins and other polyphenols scavenge free radicals in lab assays.
quick.risks: No specific safety concerns with oral extract have been reported, but regulators have acted against unsupported health claims in marketing. Responses vary between people because gut microbiota differ.

chain: Supplies ellagitannins and anthocyanins with antioxidant activity
Gut bacteria convert ellagitannins to urolithins
Aim of fewer pigmented spots, firmer and better-hydrated skin
angle.text: Pomegranate extract is taken orally and applied topically in the hope of more even, firmer and better-hydrated skin. A 2026 randomized trial in women with facial hyperpigmentation reported changes in melanin index, hydration and elasticity at some dose levels, though the primary pigmentation endpoint was not statistically significant [12].
